tagline: Into the pines at Batsto, out to the salt marsh.
intro: The byway goes into the pines at Batsto, on CR 542 in Wharton State Forest, and runs a long way under forest. One branch follows the Mullica River out to Great Bay and Tuckerton, crossing salt marsh beside the Forsythe refuge. The others turn south past the ruins of old furnaces and glassworks toward the Maurice River.

The furnaces burned the forest for fuel, and the country turned to truck farming and then to berries. At Woodbine, Jewish settlers from Poland and Russia arrived in 1891 and cleared the woods within two years. The middle of town still keeps the grid laid out that first year.

moments.title: Batsto Village
moments.text: Batsto takes its name from the Swedish for a bathing place, though its furnace, fed on bog ore dug from the streams, made cannonballs for Washington's army.

moments.title: Tuckerton Seaport
moments.text: On Tuckerton Creek a boardwalk joins 17 historic and recreated buildings of a maritime village, opened in 2000 on ground once slated for a motel and marina.

moments.title: Mauricetown
moments.text: Mauricetown, pronounced Morristown, stands on high ground above the Maurice River, a coastal-trade and shipbuilding town whose houses mostly date from 1790 to 1900.

sources.label: New Jersey Pinelands Commission, Pine Barrens Byway
